I found that in my case this is caused by an event filtering due to a directory mismatch.
In `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/context/event.ts` in `export function useEvent() {`
we have

```
      if (event.directory === project.instance.directory())
```
which failed, resulting in dropping whatever is returned from the server.

Although this is mostly caused by something I am implementing myself: using a different directory for different agents, the core problem seems to be that we CAN have multiple Instance's, each with their own directory, but a session only stores a single directory in the database; so that a desync is bound to happen at some point after a resume.

At any rate - don't consider the fact that I saw this as a bug in opencode core; this is non vanilla opencode that I'm experiencing this on. But at least this shows one possible reason for why @quliangtao038 sees this: they might also seeing an event filter at that point (due to some other reason).

This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #17801: Same root cause — custom project icons are not persisted to the backend database and rely on local storage, causing icons to disappear after restart/refresh. That issue is specific to the desktop app, but the underlying cause (missing `icon_override` persistence) appears identical.

Closing this out -- after resizing my icons down to 128x128 pixels before uploading, the file sizes were small enough that the base64 data URLs no longer overflow `localStorage`. All 8 icons now persist across refreshes.

That said, the underlying issue still exists: user-uploaded icons are only stored in `localStorage` rather than the backend database, so users with larger images or more projects will hit this same ceiling. But the 128px workaround is good enough for my case.

It seems that duplicate DNS-SD PTR (same service instance name) results causes only one advertiser to be visible on the LAN. I'm not sure if it's my setup specific (avahi daemon), but this could be avoided by generatin the PTR from the domain, not only port.

This still looks more like an upstream **Bun** issue than an OpenCode-only one.

We’ve now got a bunch of similar OpenCode reports: #8785, #13282, #14204, #16469, #10992, #14724, #15352, and #12410. There are also older examples like #5901 and #6638. A lot of these include `bun.report` links or the `oh no: Bun has crashed` message.

I've bookmarked: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues?q=repo%3Aanomalyco%2Fopencode+is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+(%22oh+no%3A+Bun+has+crashed%22+OR+bun.report+OR+%22Segmentation+fault%22)

Because these crashes can be intermittent and hard to reproduce, I suspect some sit around for a long time and then get auto-closed without the real root cause being fixed.

I think these should continue to be reported, but also reported to Bun team. Hopefully Bun will fix up stream and OpenCode team will include in future releases of OpenCode. 

@dilinzel-ine one thing that has seemed to allow me to work again and **reduced** the crashes for me was a clean reinstall:

```bash
pkill -f opencode || true

rm -rf ~/.opencode
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode
rm -rf ~/.cache/bun
rm -rf ~/.bun

npm uninstall -g opencode-ai
npm install -g opencode-ai
```

Modify for your Operating System's commands.

I just experienced the exact same issue - a single log file grew to **33GB** within 23 hours of an OpenCode session running overnight.

## My Case

| Component | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| OpenCode | 1.4.3 |
| OS | WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows (D drive) |
| Log file |  |
| Duration | ~23 hours (00:54:50 to 23:35:47) |
| Size | **33GB** (1,205,817 lines, ~27KB avg per line) |
| Skills installed | ~150+ |
| D drive impact | 98% full (294G/301G) - caused WSL instability |

## Root Cause Confirmed

The log tail shows exactly the pattern described in this issue:

INFO  2026-04-13T15:35:13 +0ms service=permission permission=skill pattern=evomap-publish ruleset=[{...hundreds of rules...}] evaluate

Every permission check dumps the entire ruleset JSON array (~27KB in my case).

## Impact

- WSL VHDX grew to 92GB
- Tabby terminal disconnected due to disk exhaustion
- Had to manually delete the 33GB log file
- Required VHDX compaction to reclaim space

## Workaround Applied

Added cron job for log cleanup:

```bash
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "0 4 * * * find ~/.local/share/opencode/log -type f -mtime +3 -delete") | crontab -
(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "30 4 * * * find ~/.local/share/opencode/log -type f -size +500M -delete") | crontab -
```

This is a critical issue that can silently exhaust disk space and crash user systems. The proposed P0 fix (remove ruleset from INFO logs or log only matched rule) would completely solve this.
